summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of depression and polysubstance use, was admitted for altered mental status, chest pain, and shortness of breath after missing five consecutive hemodialysis sessions due to losing hope and stopping his medications. He presented with volume overload, uremic encephalopathy, pruritus, and tachycardia. His symptoms improved with daily hemodialysis, which resolved his confusion, chest pain, and dyspnea. His mood improved with initiation of sertraline and engagement in outpatient psychiatric therapy. Laboratory trends showed transient thrombocytopenia that resolved, and his metabolic acidosis and hyperkalemia improved with dialysis. He was stabilized on adjusted medications, including reduced insulin and lisinopril doses, and discharged home in stable condition with services, committed to resuming dialysis and medication adherence.
